---
title: "Secrets and Sensitive Ground"
---

::: {.quest-dialog}
**Prerequisites:** Rules of the Carapace. **Objective:** keep keys, settings and sensitive data out of the agent's reach, and know what changes on a shared cluster.
**Time:** about 15 minutes. <span class="ao-badge">General practice, not a vendor claim. Your own data agreement and cluster policy override anything here.</span>
:::

Much research data is not sensitive. Some of it is, and then special agreements apply. This quest does not use any real data. It is about **habits**, so that the careful choice is automatic.

## Three ideas

1. **A prompt may leave your machine.** With a hosted model, anything the agent reads may be sent to the provider. A model running locally (the Pet, via Ollama) keeps prompts on your machine, though web or tool calls it makes may not. Whether either is allowed for your data is decided by your agreement, not by convenience.
2. **Secrets are not content.** API keys, tokens, SSH keys and passwords belong in a secret store, kept out of the project folder, and out of chats and any instructions file you commit. Be aware that an environment variable is visible to any command the agent runs, so a read rule alone is not a seal.
3. **A shared cluster is shared.** What is fine on your laptop can disturb other people on a login node, or break a data policy on shared storage. Cluster rules apply to agents exactly as they apply to you.

::: {.callout-note}
A deny rule on your secrets files (see *Rules of the Carapace*) stops the agent's file-reading tool. An agent that can run shell commands may still be able to read them another way, so also keep secrets out of the project folder, and use a sandbox or shell rules where you can. Not confirmed here: exactly how each tool treats shell reads of denied files.
:::

## Honour-system side quest

Nobody checks this and nothing depends on it. It is here because the real rules are in a document your group holds, and this site cannot see it.

<div data-ao-honour="find-agreement" data-xp="20">Find the data-handling agreement or policy that applies to your project (or ask your group leader where it is). Read the passages about <strong>where data may be processed</strong> and <strong>whether it may be sent to external services</strong>, and write down in your own notes what they say.</div>

<div data-ao-honour="find-secrets" data-xp="10">List where your own API keys and settings files live (for example a <code>.env</code> file or a shell profile), and check that your agent's permission rules deny reading them.</div>
